newsitem.title: GERMANY: German, French Telecoms want Sprint majority - report.
newsitem.headline: German, French Telecoms want Sprint majority - report.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG and France Telecom want to take a majority stake in U.S. telephone company Sprint, a partner in their global alliance, a German magazine said on Sunday.
Focus magazine said the Deutsche Telekom management board had agreed at the beginning of May on seeking the deal that could be worth about 15 billion marks.
The magazine also said Japanese telephone company NTT wanted to join the Global One alliance between the German and French telecommunications groups and Sprint that was started in January 1996.
The deal with NTT calls for the Japanese telecommunications group and Deutsche Telekom to buy 10 percent stakes in one another, the magazine said.
A Telekom spokesman declined comment on the report.
The Global One alliance was formed when Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom each bought 10 percent stakes in Sprint for a combined price of $3.7 billion.
